text: PART 4 - BASICS: your first medical fine-tune (data -> .jsonl -> QLoRA SFT -> test -> publish)
BEFORE YOU START: what you will build in this part

You will create 6 files by hand, run them in order, and end with your first trained adapter (sft-qa) that answers medical exam questions in a fixed format, published on the Hugging Face Hub and copied to (Fake)S3.

01_download_data.py  -> data/raw/*.jsonl        (7 files, untouched copies of the datasets)
02_build_sft_jsonl.py -> data/sft/*.jsonl       (9 files: qa / notes / summary x train / val / test)
                       data/pref/*.jsonl        (3 files of prompts kept aside for DPO in Part 6A)
03_validate_jsonl.py  -> "ALL_OK"               (proof the files are correct before using the GPU)
10_train_sft.py       -> outputs/adapters/sft-qa (your first LoRA adapter)
11_chat_test.py       -> base vs fine-tuned answers side by side
12_push_to_hub.py     -> your adapter on huggingface.co
The four datasets (all open, all free):

rows: US medical licensing exam questions, correct letter only
Indian medical entrance exam questions with expert explanations
research abstract + yes/no/maybe question + long answer
case reports with a doctor-patient conversation and a JSON summary

text: What one training example looks like after Step 4.5 (this is a REAL line from the data):

{"task": "qa", "source": "medmcqa", "answer_letter": "C",
 "messages": [
  {"role": "system", "content": "You are MedScriptAI, a careful medical education assistant. ..."},
  {"role": "user", "content": "A patient presents with symptoms of Hypoglycemia. ... C-peptide ... normal levels ...

Options:
A) Insulinoma
B) Accidental sulfonylurea ingestion
C) Accidental exogenous Insulin administration
D) Accidental Metformin ingestion"},
  {"role": "assistant", "content": "Answer: C) Accidental exogenous Insulin administration
Explanation: ... C peptide ... is suppressed ..."}]}
This "messages" format (system, user, assistant) is the conversational format that TRL, Unsloth and vLLM all understand.
Time and cost: about 1.5 GPU-hours (about US$2). The training run itself is roughly 10-15 minutes on an A100 (estimate; your progress bar shows the real speed).
SECTION 4.1 - Create scripts/common.py (settings shared by every script)
WHERE: VS Code Explorer (left panel), folder scripts
GOAL: one file that holds folder paths, model names and the three system prompts.
Step 1. Right-click the folder scripts.
Step 2. Click New File...
Step 3. Type common.py and press Enter.
Step 4. Paste the grey box below (Ctrl+V).
Step 5. Press Ctrl+S.

"""Shared settings and helpers used by every MedScriptAI script."""
import json                      # read/write JSON text
import os                        # read environment variables
from pathlib import Path         # build file paths that work on any OS

# Project folders. ROOT is the repo folder (one level above scripts/).
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DATA = ROOT / "data"             # all datasets live here
RAW = DATA / "raw"               # untouched downloads
SFT = DATA / "sft"               # chat-format .jsonl for SFT
PREF = DATA / "pref"             # preference pairs for DPO
OUT = ROOT / "outputs"           # adapters, predictions, reports

# Base model. The unsloth mirror is ungated; you still must accept Meta's licence.
BASE_MODEL = os.getenv("BASE_MODEL", "unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct")
BASE_MODEL_4BIT = os.getenv("BASE_MODEL_4BIT", "unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-bnb-4bit")

# One system prompt per task = one LoRA adapter per task.
SYSTEM = {
    "qa": (
        "You are MedScriptAI, a careful medical education assistant. "
        "Answer the multiple-choice question. First line: 'Answer: <letter>) <option>'. "
        "Then give a short explanation. Educational use only, not medical advice."
    ),
    "notes": (
        "You are MedScriptAI, a clinical documentation assistant. "
        "Write a concise clinical case note from the doctor-patient conversation. "
        "Use only facts stated in the conversation. Do not invent findings."
    ),
    "summary": (
        "You are MedScriptAI, a clinical information extractor. "
        "Return ONLY valid JSON that summarises the clinical note. "
        "Include only fields that are stated in the note."
    ),
}


def write_jsonl(path, rows):
    """Write a list of dicts to a .jsonl file (one JSON object per line)."""
    path = Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)       # create folders if missing
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for row in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(rows):>6} rows -> {path.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def read_jsonl(path):
    """Read a .jsonl file back into a list of dicts."""
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]


def chat(task, user, assistant=None):
    """Build the 'messages' list in the chat format TRL and vLLM understand."""
    msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM[task]},
            {"role": "user", "content": user}]
    if assistant is not None:
        msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": assistant})
    return msgs

rows: standard Python tools: JSON text, environment variables, file paths that work on every OS
the project folder = two levels above this file (scripts/common.py -> medscriptai)
one variable per folder, so no script hard-codes a path
the 16-bit base model; os.getenv lets you override it with an environment variable without editing code
the same model already compressed to 4-bit NF4 by Unsloth (5.7 GB download instead of 16 GB)
one system prompt per task; one task = one adapter. The API in Part 6A imports this SAME dict, so training and serving prompts can never differ
writes a list of dicts, one JSON object per line; `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` creates missing folders
dict -> JSON text; ensure_ascii=False keeps symbols such as °C readable
progress message; `:>6` right-aligns the number in 6 characters
reads a .jsonl file back into a list of dicts; `if line.strip()` skips empty lines
builds the messages list: system, user and (for training rows) the assistant answer

"""Step 1: download the open medical datasets and save them untouched as .jsonl."""
import argparse                                   # read command-line options
from datasets import load_dataset                 # Hugging Face dataset loader
from common import RAW                            # data/raw folder

# name on the Hub, config, split, file we save, rows to keep as (start, end) after a seeded shuffle
SOURCES = [
    ("GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options", None, "train", "medqa_train", None),
    ("GBaker/MedQA-USMLE-4-options", None, "test", "medqa_test", None),
    ("openlifescienceai/medmcqa", None, "train", "medmcqa_train", (0, 20000)),
    ("openlifescienceai/medmcqa", None, "train", "medmcqa_dpo", (20000, 23000)),  # unseen prompts for DPO
    ("openlifescienceai/medmcqa", None, "validation", "medmcqa_val", None),
    ("qiaojin/PubMedQA", "pqa_labeled", "train", "pubmedqa", None),
    ("AGBonnet/augmented-clinical-notes", None, "train", "clinical_notes", (0, 12000)),
]

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=None, help="tiny test run: keep N rows per file")
args = parser.parse_args()

RAW.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)            # make data/raw if it does not exist
for name, config, split, out_name, rows in SOURCES:
    ds = load_dataset(name, config, split=split)  # downloads once, then uses the local cache
    if rows:                                      # same seed = same order, so slices never overlap
        ds = ds.shuffle(seed=42).select(range(rows[0], min(rows[1], len(ds))))
    if args.limit:                                # --limit: tiny test run
        ds = ds.select(range(min(args.limit, len(ds))))
    path = RAW / f"{out_name}.jsonl"
    ds.to_json(str(path), lines=True, force_ascii=False)  # one JSON object per line
    print(f"{out_name:16} {len(ds):>6} rows  <- {name} [{split}]")

rows: lets you pass options such as --limit on the command line
Hugging Face's loader: downloads once, caches in HF_HOME, returns a table
the shopping list: Hub name, sub-set name, split, output file name, rows to keep
MedQA training questions; None = keep all rows
MedMCQA: keep rows 0-19,999 after shuffling (the full set has 182k; 20k is plenty)
3,000 DIFFERENT MedMCQA questions kept aside for DPO, so they are new to the SFT model
12,000 clinical notes with conversations and JSON summaries
optional tiny test run: keep only N rows per file
create data/raw (no error if it exists)
download the first time, load from the cache afterwards
shuffle with a fixed seed (same order every run) and take a slice; same seed = the SFT slice and the DPO slice never overlap
save as .jsonl (lines=True = one object per line)

BEFORE YOU START: what this script does. Raw datasets all look different (MedQA has an options dict, MedMCQA has opa/opb/opc/opd columns, PubMedQA has abstracts). This script converts every row into the same "messages" format, removes broken rows, removes duplicates, makes sure no test question is in training, and writes train/val/test files. GOAL: proof that every line is valid chat data and fits in 2048 tokens.

"""Step 3: prove every .jsonl file is valid chat data before you pay for GPU time."""
import json                                         # parse each line
import statistics                                   # median / max token counts
import sys                                          # exit code for pass/fail
from pathlib import Path
from common import SFT, BASE_MODEL

ROLES = ["system", "user", "assistant"]
errors = 0

try:                                                # token counts need the Llama tokenizer
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(BASE_MODEL)
except Exception as exc:                            # still validate structure without it
    tok = None
    print(f"(tokenizer not loaded, skipping token counts: {exc.__class__.__name__})")

for path in sorted(Path(SFT).glob("*.jsonl")):
    lengths = []
    for n, line in enumerate(path.open(encoding="utf-8"), start=1):
        try:
            row = json.loads(line)                  # 1) each line must be valid JSON
            roles = [m["role"] for m in row["messages"]]
            assert roles == ROLES, f"roles {roles}"  # 2) exactly system -> user -> assistant
            assert all(m["content"].strip() for m in row["messages"]), "empty message"
            if row["task"] == "summary":            # 3) summary targets must be valid JSON
                json.loads(row["messages"][-1]["content"])
            if tok:                                 # 4) length in tokens after the chat template
                ids = tok.apply_chat_template(row["messages"], tokenize=True)
                ids = ids["input_ids"] if isinstance(ids, dict) or hasattr(ids, "keys") else ids
                lengths.append(len(ids))
        except Exception as exc:
            errors += 1
            print(f"ERROR {path.name}:{n}: {exc}")
    stats = f" tokens median={statistics.median(lengths):.0f} max={max(lengths)}" if lengths else ""
    print(f"{path.name:22} rows={n:>6}{stats}")

print("ALL_OK" if errors == 0 else f"FAILED with {errors} errors")
sys.exit(1 if errors else 0)

rows: loads Llama-3.1's real tokenizer to count tokens; if that fails, structure is still checked
check 4: the summary target is valid JSON
check 5: the real token count after Llama's chat template
newer transformers return a dict, older a list; this handles both

SECTION 4.7 - Create scripts/10_train_sft.py (the training script)

BEFORE YOU START: what happens when you run it. (1) The 4-bit Llama model (5.7 GB) is downloaded and loaded on the GPU. (2) LoRA adapters (about 42 million trainable numbers) are attached. (3) Each training example is turned into one long text with the chat template. (4) The trainer runs 125 steps (2,000 examples / 16 per step); every 10 steps it prints the loss, every 100 steps the validation loss. (5) Only the adapter (about 80-170 MB) is saved to outputs/adapters/sft-qa. GPU memory used: roughly 10-16 GB of the 80 GB.
WHERE: VS Code Explorer, folder scripts
GOAL: the QLoRA SFT training script.
Step 1. Right-click the folder scripts.
Step 2. Click New File...
Step 3. Type 10_train_sft.py and press Enter.
Step 4. Paste the grey box below.
Step 5. Press Ctrl+S.

"""Step 4: QLoRA supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with Unsloth + TRL + PEFT.

One run = one task = one LoRA adapter, e.g.  python scripts/10_train_sft.py --task qa
"""
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel                    # import Unsloth FIRST so it can patch TRL/transformers
from unsloth.chat_templates import train_on_responses_only

import argparse                                          # command-line options
import json                                              # save the training log
from datasets import load_dataset                        # read our .jsonl files
from trl import SFTConfig, SFTTrainer                    # Hugging Face TRL trainer
from common import SFT, OUT, BASE_MODEL_4BIT

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--task", required=True, choices=["qa", "notes", "summary"])
p.add_argument("--max-train", type=int, default=None, help="use only the first N training rows")
p.add_argument("--epochs", type=float, default=1.0)
p.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=-1, help="stop after N steps (-1 = use epochs)")
p.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)        # LoRA learns fast; 2e-4 is the usual QLoRA rate
p.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=16)          # LoRA rank r: size of the adapter matrices
p.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=8)          # examples per GPU step
p.add_argument("--grad-accum", type=int, default=2)     # effective batch = batch x grad-accum = 16
p.add_argument("--train-file", default=None, help="override the training .jsonl (Part 5 uses this)")
p.add_argument("--run-name", default=None)
a = p.parse_args()
run = a.run_name or f"sft-{a.task}"
out_dir = OUT / "adapters" / run

# 1) Load the base model already quantised to 4-bit (this is the "Q" in QLoRA).
model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name=BASE_MODEL_4BIT,     # 4-bit NF4 weights: ~5.7 GB on disk instead of ~16 GB
    max_seq_length=2048,            # longest example we keep is ~1,600 tokens
    load_in_4bit=True,
    dtype=None,                     # None = auto: bfloat16 on A100/L40/H100
)

# 2) Attach small trainable LoRA matrices to every attention and MLP projection.
model = FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model(
    model,
    r=a.rank,
    lora_alpha=a.rank,              # scaling = alpha / r = 1.0
    lora_dropout=0.0,               # 0 is fastest in Unsloth and works well
    target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"],
    use_gradient_checkpointing="unsloth",   # recompute activations to save VRAM
    random_state=3407,
)
model.print_trainable_parameters()  # expect ~42M trainable of ~8B (about 0.5%)


# 3) Turn each {"messages": [...]} row into one string using Llama-3.1's own chat template.
#    The template starts with <|begin_of_text|>; the trainer adds it again when tokenising,
#    so we remove it here to end up with exactly ONE begin token (double BOS hurts quality).
def to_text(batch):
    texts = [tokenizer.apply_chat_template(m, tokenize=False).removeprefix(tokenizer.bos_token)
             for m in batch["messages"]]
    return {"text": texts}


train_file = a.train_file or str(SFT / f"{a.task}_train.jsonl")
train = load_dataset("json", data_files=train_file, split="train")
if a.max_train:
    train = train.select(range(min(a.max_train, len(train))))
val = load_dataset("json", data_files=str(SFT / f"{a.task}_val.jsonl"), split="train").select(range(100))
train = train.map(to_text, batched=True, remove_columns=train.column_names)
val = val.map(to_text, batched=True, remove_columns=val.column_names)
print(train[0]["text"][:600])       # eyeball one formatted example before spending GPU time

# 4) Training settings.
cfg = SFTConfig(
    output_dir=str(OUT / "checkpoints" / run),
    dataset_text_field="text",
    max_length=2048,
    per_device_train_batch_size=a.batch,
    gradient_accumulation_steps=a.grad_accum,
    num_train_epochs=a.epochs,
    max_steps=a.max_steps,
    learning_rate=a.lr,
    lr_scheduler_type="cosine",     # smooth decay to ~0 by the end
    warmup_steps=10,                # ramp the LR up for the first 10 steps
    optim="adamw_8bit",             # 8-bit optimiser states: big VRAM saving
    weight_decay=0.01,
    bf16=True,
    logging_steps=10,
    eval_strategy="steps",
    eval_steps=100,
    save_steps=200,
    save_total_limit=2,             # keep only the 2 newest checkpoints on disk
    report_to="none",
    seed=3407,
)
trainer = SFTTrainer(model=model, processing_class=tokenizer, train_dataset=train,
                     eval_dataset=val, args=cfg)

# 5) Only learn from the assistant's answer, not from the system/user text.
trainer = train_on_responses_only(
    trainer,
    instruction_part="<|start_header_id|>user<|end_header_id|>\n\n",
    response_part="<|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>\n\n",
)

stats = trainer.train()

# 6) Save ONLY the adapter (~80-170 MB at r=16), not the 16 GB base model.
model.save_pretrained(str(out_dir))
tokenizer.save_pretrained(str(out_dir))
(out_dir / "train_log.json").write_text(json.dumps(trainer.state.log_history, indent=1))
print(f"DONE adapter={out_dir} train_loss={stats.training_loss:.4f}")

"""Step 5: ask the same test questions to the base model and to base + your adapter, side by side."""
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel                    # Unsloth first, as always

import argparse
import torch
from common import SFT, OUT, read_jsonl

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--task", default="qa", choices=["qa", "notes", "summary"])
p.add_argument("--adapter", default=None, help="adapter folder (default outputs/adapters/sft-<task>)")
p.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=3, help="how many test examples to show")
a = p.parse_args()
adapter = a.adapter or str(OUT / "adapters" / f"sft-{a.task}")

# Loading the ADAPTER folder makes Unsloth read adapter_config.json, load the 4-bit base, then attach the LoRA.
model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(adapter, max_seq_length=2048, load_in_4bit=True)
FastLanguageModel.for_inference(model)                    # switch on Unsloth's fast generation path


def answer(messages):
    """Greedy-decode one reply for a list of chat messages (system + user)."""
    ids = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt",
                                        return_dict=True).to("cuda")
    out = model.generate(**ids, max_new_tokens=400, do_sample=False)   # do_sample=False = deterministic
    return tokenizer.decode(out[0][ids["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True).strip()


for row in read_jsonl(SFT / f"{a.task}_test.jsonl")[: a.n]:
    prompt = row["messages"][:2]                           # system + user only; hide the reference answer
    with model.disable_adapter():                          # temporarily turn LoRA OFF = plain base model
        base = answer(prompt)
    tuned = answer(prompt)                                 # LoRA back ON
    print("=" * 80, "\nUSER:", prompt[1]["content"][:500])
    print("\n--- BASE ---\n", base[:700])
    print("\n--- FINE-TUNED ---\n", tuned[:700])
    print("\n--- REFERENCE ---\n", row["messages"][2]["content"][:700])
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

rows: pointing at the ADAPTER folder: Unsloth reads adapter_config.json, loads the 4-bit base and attaches your LoRA
switch Unsloth to its fast generation mode
format system + user and end with the assistant header so the model starts answering
greedy decoding: always the most likely token, repeatable
keep only the new tokens (cut the prompt)
system + user; the reference answer is hidden
temporarily switch LoRA OFF = the plain base model
free cached GPU memory between examples

"""Step 6: publish an adapter or a dataset folder to the Hugging Face Hub (private by default)."""
import argparse
from huggingface_hub import HfApi                  # official Hub client; reads HF_TOKEN from the environment

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("--folder", required=True, help="local folder, e.g. outputs/adapters/sft-qa or data/sft")
p.add_argument("--repo", required=True, help="YOUR_HF_USERNAME/Llama-3.1-8B-MedScriptAI-qa-lora")
p.add_argument("--type", default="model", choices=["model", "dataset"])
p.add_argument("--public", action="store_true", help="make the repo public (default private)")
a = p.parse_args()

api = HfApi()
api.create_repo(a.repo, repo_type=a.type, private=not a.public, exist_ok=True)   # no error if it exists
api.upload_folder(folder_path=a.folder, repo_id=a.repo, repo_type=a.type,
                  ignore_patterns=["checkpoint-*", "*.pt", "optimizer*"])          # skip training leftovers
print(f"https://huggingface.co/{'datasets/' if a.type == 'dataset' else ''}{a.repo}")

PART 4 RESULT CHECK
4.13 Common mistake at this level

The mistake: training on text formatted differently from what the server sends later (two <|begin_of_text|> tokens, a different system prompt, or a missing chat template). The model then underperforms and you blame the hyper-parameters.

How to spot it: print one formatted training example (10_train_sft.py does this), print what your API sends (Part 6A), and compare them. This project avoids it by importing SYSTEM from scripts/common.py everywhere and by the removeprefix fix.
